purpose: Recover the horizontal/vertical follow ordering at camera reference-tile rebases.

evidence.next_frame: MAME advances to camera x=1071 with one follow service; it does not perform the legacy queued double-follow.
evidence.native_result: Horizontal follow runs on the rebase frame, vertical follow is suppressed only there, the player VM still ticks, and no extra catch-up follow runs. These fields match through aligned frame 394.
evidence.remaining_boundary: At aligned frame 395 MAME exposes CAMERA_UPDATE_DELAY=6 and interaction_lock=0x28 after an actor-collision/cleanup transition; the native actor table is already divergent at frame 27, so this side effect remains coupled to the unresolved actor scheduler.

implementation.camera_api: Engine::update_camera(bool suppress_vertical_follow) separates the two independent damped lookups.
implementation.rebase_order: Vertical reference rebases call horizontal follow immediately, then resume ordinary vertical follow on the next pass.
implementation.animation_order: The player animation VM is not deferred at a vertical rebase boundary.

conclusion: Camera reference-tile rebasing is not a full-pass skip or a queued double-follow: horizontal follow and the player VM still run on the rebase boundary, while only the vertical damped lookup is deferred.
